title: E-RLT-0062: symmetry by schedule does not give the $k^4$ law, partial: cycling the first-mirror knit through its 576...
purpose: Experiment E-RLT-0062 in the relativity arena: symmetry by schedule does not give the $k^4$ law, partial: cycling the first-mirror knit through its 576 W(F4) conjugates, the exact period group is {I, -I} (coset combinatorics, exhaustive), which forces nothing; run forward then back (period 1,152) it keeps exact CPT at mirror 1,151, run once through it has none, while every beat keeps CPT alone; the husk charge, trace and shear anisotropies stay finite as k falls (exponent 0.00 for both orders, charge 0.0050, trace 0.0010, shear 0.022) where the base knit holds 0.68, 0.31, 0.82 and the W(F4)-averaged matrix falls as $k^4$: averaging over the schedule shrinks the leading anisotropy 137-fold in charge and leaves it; partial because the Rayleigh-Ritz cross-check gate failed on its period-one case (0.71), a case the method cannot resolve and the readings did not use; on 24- and 96-beat pieces it agrees to 4e-13.
known_limitations: Depth L2 (L2: known physics reproduced on a stated model).
